correctness.rationale: The published linear-kernel cross-HSIC and jackknife formulas reduce exactly to \(T_n=\operatorname{sgn}(f_2)(n-2)C/\sqrt{n(n-1)Q}\). Gaussian centering gives independent Haar directions on the centered sphere. The \(n=3\) identity is exact. For \(n=4\) an exact rational Jacobian minor is \(-15/16\) before harmless global normalizations; for \(n\ge5\) the quartic-root annihilator argument proves a regular denominator zero. The submersion theorem then gives a \(t^{-(n-1)}\) lower-tail neighborhood and hence divergence of absolute moments \(p\ge n-1\). Computation is supplemental, not the proof.

value.rationale: The theorem exposes a structural finite-sample feature of a Gaussian-calibrated self-normalized independence statistic: bounded arcsine behavior at \(n=3\) changes to regular denominator singularities from \(n=4\) onward, producing unbounded support and missing high moments. This is mathematically motivated by calibration and by the use of moment approximations for studentized statistics, rather than by an arbitrary parameter slice.
